body:
This is native to browsers and mobile clients. Most client side libraries force this. This is not something developers typically need to handle, at all. I suggest we drop it.

| # | Description | 
| :---: | :--- | 
| **9.2.6** | [ADDED] Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server. |

comments.body: I understand that this is intended to apply to all sort of clients, especially communications between the application and external services (when the application is acting as a client). This is corroborated by the fact that this is in the "General **Service to Service** Communication Security".
My take on this is - the client side HTTP/S libraries handle this automatically and as a developer I almost never have to check this. Even for server-to-server communications.

Google: `curl_setopt verify peer ssl host site:stackoverflow.com` - this is quite often done the way that ssl verification is "turned off".

I can see a clear reason why the requirement must stay.
